answers.explanation: Resilience covers the whole incident. Systems do go down; resilient ones keep the critical parts working and recover.
Up isn't the same as useful. A server can answer while its data is corrupted, or be up only because nothing has tested it yet.
Redundancy: a second disk, server, link, or supplier ready to replace the one that failed.
Resourcefulness: when you can't run everything, run what matters most.
Rapidity is measured by recovery time: how long until everything is back.
Robustness is how much a system can take before it stops working.
Depth times duration. A shallower or narrower dip means a cheaper incident.
Rapidity shortens recovery, so the dip ends sooner. Robustness makes it shallower.
Partial restoration counts, like checkout back at half capacity. Degrees of restoration are worth measuring.
Money and customers are what managers decide with. Turning downtime into lost orders makes the case for spending.
